sources.title: Marine Personnel Regulations, SOR/2007-115 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-12-20; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Text of the relevant sections was read from the official consolidated XML (Open Government Licence - Canada, LICENSE.md seen). Sections read: 1-2 (application), 100 (list of certificates; Master, Limited is 100(h)), 103 (5-year validity of MED/SEN courses and equivalents; first aid and passenger-vessel courses are not valid for life), 106 (renewal of a 100(h) certificate: sea service on the vessel and area, or refresher MED plus practical and oral exam on general seamanship, or marine-related service), 110 (age 18 at issue, sea service started at 16, application at least 2 weeks before the first exam, valid 1 year), 111 (medical certificate needed for a s.131 certificate only if the vessel is passenger-carrying), 112-113 (TP 2293 exam procedure; pass valid 5 years, then for life once the certificate is issued), 115 (8 hours = 1 day; 12-hour watch = 1.5 days; months = days / 30), 120(2)(m) (Master, Limited not STCW-endorsed), 121 (fees: oral/practical for a limited certificate $27.50, written exam $27.50), 130 (Master, Limited 60 GT or more, for contrast: SEN Limited if radar fitted), 131 (Master, Limited less than 60 GT: 2 months deck sea service on vessels of at least the same GT and voyage type, or 1 month approved on-board training; MED by vessel type; radio operator certificate if VHF fitted; marine basic first aid; exams per TP 2293), 205-206 (MED for crew, first aid person, familiarization and training records), 210-216 (manning, master and deck watch composition), 212 Table 1 item 16 (certificate valid as master on vessels under 60 GT of a type, tonnage, area and period of operation specified, near coastal Class 2 and sheltered waters only), 244-254, 319-322 (hours of rest). Not the official version; check the live Justice Laws text before release.

sources.title: Small Vessel Regulations, SOR/2010-91 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2026-01-19, last amended 2025-12-31 (includes SOR/2025-272); repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Part titles read, and Part 4 (passenger-carrying vessels of not more than 15 GT carrying not more than 12 passengers, ss. 400-420) read in full: passenger safety briefing items and lifejacket demonstration (401), reporting persons on board to a designated person ashore (402), hypothermia/cold-shock protection when water is below 15 degrees C and no life raft (403), notice to the Minister before first service (405), equipment tables by length: personal life-saving appliances (409), visual signals (410), life rafts (411, not needed if 8.5 m or less, sheltered waters, or within 2 nm of shore of a river or lake), anchor and rope lengths and bilge pumps (412), navigation equipment (413), extinguisher ratings (414), engine-space discharge port and CO2 quantity 1.2 kg per cubic metre (415-416), detectors with 84 dB alarms (418), emergency procedures and crew practice (420). Part 5 (workboats), Part 6 (critical safety requirements), Part 7 (construction, stability adequate for intended operations) and Part 10 were only skimmed. Recent amendments (SOR/2025-272) changed Part 1; check Parts 4 and 5 again before writing.

sources.title: Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, SOR/2020-216 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-12-20; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read: Part 1 ss. 102-125 (equipment: standard magnetic compass, exception for vessels 8 m or less within sight of marks; steering compass allowed under 150 GT; deviation table near compass; GNSS and spare compass at 150 GT; radar, echo sounder and ATA/ARPA at 300 GT; AIS Class A at 20 m (non-pleasure), more than 50 passengers, towboats 8 m or more; AIS A or B for passenger vessels and for vessels 8 m or more carrying a passenger outside sheltered waters; AIS on 30 min before departure; hand lead line at 20 m; towboat radar at 5 GT on inland/NC2), ss. 138-146 (charts and publications list, exception for under 100 GT with sufficient local knowledge, ECDIS conditions, voyage planning per IMO A.893(21), plotting and monitoring position, charts corrected from Notices to Mariners), Part 2 ss. 200-254 (radio definitions incl. sea areas A1-A4; VHF-DSC carriage for vessels over 8 m, carrying passengers or towboats; EPIRB carriage; NAVTEX; documents incl. RAMN and TP 9878 card; radio record kept 12 months; time in local time or UTC on international voyages; continuous listening watch from 15 minutes before underway; navigation safety call circumstances, content order and 1-minute limit), Schedule 4 (Channel 16 outside traffic zones, the VTS channel inside). Not the official version; check live text before release.

sources.title: Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations, SOR/2012-69 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-12-29, last amended 2021-06-23; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read: definitions (garbage, oily mixture, ppm, sewage), s. 30 (oily mixture may be discharged in Section I waters only en route, through MARPOL oil filtering equipment producing 15 ppm or less, with alarm and stop at 5 ppm in inland waters or 15 ppm elsewhere), ss. 94-96 (sewage: through a marine sanitation device with fecal coliform 250/100 mL, or 14/100 mL in a designated sewage area; for vessels under 400 GT not certified for more than 15 persons, comminuted and disinfected at 1 nm or more, or untreated at 3 nm or more en route at the fastest feasible speed, with rules for narrow waters), ss. 100-101 (garbage discharge rules outside Section I waters: 25 nm for floating dunnage, 12 nm for other non-plastic garbage, 3 nm if ground to 25 mm). The Section I/II waters definitions were not read; confirm before writing that garbage discharge is prohibited in Section I waters.

sources.title: Canada Shipping Act, 2001, S.C. 2001, c. 26 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-06-22; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read: s. 17 (every Canadian maritime document is valid for the period the Minister specifies), ss. 105-118 (duties of authorized representative: meet regulations, develop safe operating and emergency procedures, ensure safety training; master: obtain documents before a voyage, safety of persons, not carry more persons than certified, do not submerge load lines, report dangers such as Beaufort force 10 or more without a warning or severe icing (s. 112); crew duties; passengers must obey directions; no jeopardizing safety), s. 126 (VTS clearance), ss. 128-133 (report damage to or malfunction of aids to navigation to MCTS without delay; SAR coordinator directions; duty to proceed to distress and record reasons in the official log if not proceeding; duty to assist persons in danger at sea), s. 148 (duty after collision: assist, stand by, exchange vessel and representative details). This is an Act, kind set to 'regulation' because the schema has no 'statute' kind.

sources.title: Transportation Safety Board Regulations, SOR/2014-37 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2018-11-23; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read s. 3 (marine occurrences that must be reported to the TSB by the operator, master, pilot, crew or harbour master with direct knowledge: death or serious injury, person overboard, incapacitation of a crew member, sinking/capsizing, collision or risk of collision, fire or explosion, grounding, bottom contact, damage affecting seaworthiness, anchoring/beaching to avoid an occurrence, missing or abandoned, fouling a cable or pipeline, total failure of navigation equipment, machinery, propulsion, steering or deck machinery, cargo shift or loss, dangerous goods release; report as soon as possible by the quickest means, remainder within 30 days; a report to an MCTS centre counts as a report to the Board).

sources.title: Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations, SOR/2021-135 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2021-06-23; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read: s. 1 voyage definitions (sheltered waters voyage; near coastal voyage, Class 2 = always within 25 nm of shore in waters contiguous to Canada, the US (not Hawaii) or St Pierre and Miquelon and within 100 nm of a place of refuge; near coastal Class 1 = up to 200 nm from shore or above the continental shelf, north of 6 degrees N; unlimited), s. 11 (Division 2 inspection-certificate regime applies to non-Convention vessels of 15 GT or less carrying more than 12 passengers and to vessels over 15 GT, not pleasure craft), Schedule 1 Part 6 (British Columbia sheltered waters, items 1 to 19, e.g. Vancouver Harbour, Fraser River, Victoria area inside Trial Islands-Albert Head, Nanaimo Harbour, Strait of Georgia east of 123 deg 22.666 min W, Howe Sound in summer, Gulf Islands passages, Sooke, Comox Harbour seasonally) and Schedule 2 Part 4 (BC ferry routes).

sources.title: Vessel Construction and Equipment Regulations, SOR/2023-257 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Only the application and grandfathering sections (ss. 4-12) and the stability references were read. Applies mainly to Safety Convention passenger vessels and to passenger and cargo vessels 24 m or more (not fishing vessels or pleasure craft), so most vessels under 60 GT are outside it. It refers to the 2008 IS Code as modified by TP 7301 (December 2023) and to TP 10943 damage stability standards. Use only to tell writers which rules do NOT apply to typical small vessels.

sources.title: Fishing Vessel Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1486 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2025-07-24, last amended 2023-12-20; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Only stability-related provisions were read (record of modifications affecting stability, s. 3.12; adequate stability of existing vessels, s. 3.45; stability assessments, ss. 3.48-3.5, with full assessments to the 2008 IS Code; no operation in a freezing spray warning area unless the stability assessment covers icing). Master, Limited is not a fishing certificate; use only for comparison and for the icing/freezing-spray fact.

sources.title: Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations, SOR/2025-275 (consolidated XML)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: In force 2026-03-31; repository commit b7292cf; read 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read ss. 1-15 and Schedule 1. These new regulations repealed the old VTS Zones Regulations (SOR/89-98) and the Northern Canada VTS Zone Regulations on 2026-03-31. General application: 300 GT or more; towing/pushing with combined 500 GT or more; vessels carrying pollutants or dangerous goods as cargo (and their tugs). In the Western VTS Zones (Victoria and Prince Rupert) the reporting sections also apply to vessels 20 m or more (except pleasure craft under 30 m and fishing vessels under 24 m and not more than 150 GT) and to tows where the combined length is 45 m or more or the tow is 20 m or more (log booming grounds excepted). Reports: sailing plan 15 minutes before entering, before a manoeuvre, or before leaving a berth; position reports at calling-in points; final report; reports of fire, collision, grounding, defects, pollution, hazards; deviation report. Content and procedure are in RAMN Part 3. Older sources (PAC 200 2022, older RAMN) describe the repealed regime.

sources.title: TP 2293E Qualifications for the Certification of Seafarers, Revision 8 draft (April 2019), third-party copy
sources.publisher: Transport Canada Marine Safety (draft), copy hosted by dieselduck.info
sources.notes: Read only through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool, which could reach roughly the first 100 000 characters (sections up to about 3.47; section 3.48 'Domestic Certificates of Competency (Limited)' was NOT reached). The tool reported the statement 'Permission is granted, by Transport Canada Marine Safety, to copy this TP 2293E, as required.' Used for: competence statements for Chartwork and Pilotage Level 1 (plan and conduct a coastal passage: chart construction, publications, position by landmarks, aids and dead reckoning with wind/tide/current, log book and compass error record), Navigation Safety Level 1 (COLREGs with Canadian modifications and the principles of keeping a navigational watch, STCW A-II/1), SEN Limited (radar, GPS, AIS, echo sounder, compass errors, ECS, phones/tablets for planning, watchkeeping, BRM, emergencies), and the 70 per cent pass mark for these TC exams. It is a DRAFT; the November 2021 Revision 8 (T29-24/2021E) is the edition to verify against.

sources.title: TP 2293E The Examination and Certification of Seafarers, Revision 5 (July 2007), third-party copy
sources.publisher: Transport Canada Marine Safety, copy hosted by dieselduck.info
sources.notes: Read only through an automated summariser that reached about 124 000 characters; Chapter 12 'Master, Limited' (about page 162; oral syllabus said by a study site to be section 12.11, pages 169-179) was NOT reached. The tool reported the copyright line with 'Permission is granted ... to copy this TP 2293E, as required' and that the pass mark for nautical written exams including NS1 and CP1 is 70 per cent. Superseded; use only as background.

sources.title: The examination and certification of seafarers (TP 2293E), Revision 8, November 2021: catalogue record T29-24/2021E-PDF
sources.notes: Only the catalogue record was read (title, revision, catalogue number, PDF link https://publications.gc.ca/collections/collection_2022/tc/T29-24-2021-eng.pdf). The PDF itself could not be fetched (proxy blocked; summariser returned an interstitial). This is the edition MPR s. 131 points to for the exam subjects; a human must read its Master, Limited chapter. TC's TP 2293 page (dated 2024-03-26) says copies are by request.

sources.title: Vessel stability training (Small Fishing Vessel Stability e-course)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. States TC and CCOHS offer a free online Small Fishing Vessel Stability e-course (free with a CDN) aimed at people without formal TC stability training, including holders of Limited Master/Chief Mate certificates, SVOP and small fishing certificates. Not listed in MPR s. 131 as a requirement; present it as recommended.

sources.title: Ship Safety Bulletin No. 16/2020: Hazards and risks of girding during towing operations
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Girding: tug pulled broadside by the towline and unable to recover, leading quickly to capsize. Risk factors: short towline, steep towline angle, tow close to the tug, speed/course changes, narrow channels. Precautions: tow plan, towing point awareness, tested emergency release, heel limits, crew training, communication.

sources.title: TP 15491 Small Vessel Compliance Program: Tug Guidance Notes (06/2024)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser (first 100 000 characters). Guidance for small tugs up to 15 GT completing the Small Vessel Detailed Compliance Report: bollard pull, towing gear and release, pre-departure checklists, girding, tow planning, stability with towing loads, watertightness, VHF/DSC, EPIRB, towing lights, searchlights, radar, voyage planning, crew familiarization, rest hours. States it does not replace the regulations.

sources.title: The Canadian Aids to Navigation System 2023
sources.publisher: Canadian Coast Guard (Fisheries and Oceans Canada)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser (first 100 000 of about 110 000 characters). Used for: IALA Region B lateral system and direction of buoyage; port hand green, flat-topped, odd numbers, green Fl 4s or Q; starboard hand red, conical, even numbers, red Fl 4s or Q; fairway red/white vertical stripes, Mo(A) 6s or LFl 10s, pass keeping it to port; bifurcation Fl(2+1); cardinal colours, topmarks and Q/VQ rhythms (N continuous, E 3, S 6+LFl, W 9); isolated danger black/red with two black spheres, Fl(2); special marks yellow Fl 4s; ODAS Fl(5)Y 20s; range daymarks; fog signals; light characteristic definitions (Q 50-79/min, VQ 80-159/min, LFl 2 s); cautions about relying on buoys. Quote nothing until the reproduction terms are checked.

sources.title: Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2025, Part 3: Vessel Traffic Services
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Gave Canada/US Cooperative VTS sectors and channels in the Juan de Fuca area (Prince Rupert Traffic Ch 74 for the west coast approaches, Seattle Traffic Ch 05A, Victoria Traffic Ch 11 for Haro Strait/Boundary Pass/south Strait of Georgia) and sailing plan contents. The summariser's participation thresholds were inconsistent with SOR/2025-275; use the regulation for thresholds and this Part for channels, calling-in points and report formats, after a human reads the current Part 3.

sources.title: Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2024, Part 5: ECCC marine and ice warning and forecast programs
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Pacific marine forecasts and technical synopsis issued 4 times daily (04:00, 10:30, 16:00, 21:30 local), NAVTEX from Prince Rupert MCTS via Amphitrite Point and Digby Island, a Weatheradio frequency list. ECCC's own Pacific page (sixty-eccc-pacific-products) says Weatheradio is no longer in service; resolve before writing about Weatheradio.

sources.title: Canadian Chart 1: Symbols, Abbreviations and Terms
sources.edition: Accessed 2026-10-06 (a 2019 PDF edition is listed in the DFO library)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser: explains chart symbols, abbreviations and terms in the common IHO lettered-section format. Writers should open the current edition themselves for each symbol taught and describe symbols in words or redraw them; do not copy CHS artwork without a licence.

sources.title: Canadian marine warning program: chapter 1
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Wind warning bands excluding gusts: strong wind 20-33 kn, gale 34-47 kn, storm 48-63 kn, hurricane force 64 kn or more; strong wind warnings are issued for coastal/inland areas in the boating season, Pacific program 20 March to 11 November. Page is old (2014); confirm current dates.

sources.title: Marine weather products and services: Pacific coast
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Products: regular marine forecast (days 1-2: wind, weather, visibility), extended forecast (days 3-5), technical marine synopsis, marine weather statement, wave height forecast, NAVTEX forecast; issue times 4 am, 10:30 am, 4 pm, 9:30 pm (extended and waves 4 am and 4 pm); access by the ECCC website, phone consultation and the Coast Guard Continuous Marine Broadcast; says Weatheradio is no longer in service.

sources.title: Beaufort wind scale table
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser: Beaufort force 0-12 with knots, descriptions and sea and land observations (e.g. force 6 strong breeze 22-27 kn, force 9 strong gale 41-47 kn, force 12 hurricane 64 kn and over). A writer must read the full table before quoting other forces.

sources.title: Weather warnings (ATSC 113 Weather for Sailing, Flying and Snow Sports)
sources.publisher: University of British Columbia, Department of Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Lists strong wind, gale, storm, hurricane force, freezing spray and squall warnings, notes that warnings state whether winds are outflow or inflow, and that strong wind warnings are seasonal. Copyrighted course material: link and paraphrase only (as the plan says).

sources.title: RIC-25 Syllabus for the Restricted Operator's Certificate - Maritime Commercial (ROC-MC)
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.edition: Issue 3, April 2008; Annex A updated April 2025; accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. ROC-MC is for operators on compulsorily fitted commercial vessels in the North American Sea Area A1 with VHF (plus exceptions for some fishing vessels 15-150 tons with MF/HF). Exam pass mark 70 per cent; course 20 hours plus review/exam; minimum age 18; valid for life. Syllabus: maritime mobile service basics and R/T procedures; GMDSS concept, MMSI, sea areas, Ch 16 and DSC watch; VHF-DSC controls and call categories; false alert cancellation; 2182 kHz; portable VHF, SART, EPIRB; NAVTEX; DSC distress alert sending, acknowledging, relay; urgency and safety calls; on-scene SAR.

sources.title: Professional radio operator certificate services: frequently asked questions
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. ROC-M is issued under delegation by the Canadian Power and Sail Squadrons and is the certificate for pleasure craft radios; an ROC-MC is also valid on pleasure craft. Does not settle which certificate a commercial master under 60 GT needs; see the brief.

sources.title: Safety practices related to small fishing vessel stability (FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Technical Paper 517)
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (A. Gudmundsson)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser (contents page and the precautions chapter PDF https://www.fao.org/docrep/pdf/011/i0625e/i0625e03b.pdf). Covers displacement, draught, freeboard, lightship, deadweight, list/heel/loll, G, B, M, stable/unstable/neutral equilibrium, stiff and tender vessels, suspended weights, free surface, watertight vs weathertight, GZ curves, dynamic stability, icing (remove ice from high up first, keep freeing ports clear), following seas, rolling period test (sufficient stability if the full roll period in seconds is less than the beam in metres; up to 1.2 x beam when fuel and stores are low). Reproduction statement allows educational or non-commercial use with acknowledgement; marked 'unclear' because the app may be commercial.

sources.title: Watchkeeping Standards (including 2010 Manila Amendments), AMSA 242
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. A government reproduction of STCW Code A-VIII/2 principles used as a secondary source because the IMO text is not freely available: factors for composing the watch, taking over the watch (relieving officer's checks; do not hand over during a manoeuvre), performing the watch, purposes of the lookout, sole lookout only in daylight after assessment and with help immediately available, when to call the master (list), restricted visibility, anchor watch duties. Canadian law applies A-VIII/2 Parts 2, 3 and 3-1 via MPR ss. 213 and 244.

sources.title: The American Practical Navigator (Bowditch), 2019 edition, Volume II, Chapter 5: Compass Conversions
sources.publisher: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (copy hosted by thenauticalalmanac.com)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. True-magnetic-compass chain; variation between true and magnetic, deviation between magnetic and compass, compass error = algebraic sum; easterly errors make compass readings lower than true, westerly higher; worked example 215 T, 7 W var, 1.5 W dev gives 222 M, 223.5 C, error 8.5 W. The front matter (same host) states 'No domestic copyright claimed under Title 17 U.S.C.'; foreign use terms not confirmed, so 'unclear'.

sources.title: Navigation course: position fixing (running fixes, doubled angle, four-point bearing, special angles, dipping range)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Secondary teaching page: doubling the angle on the bow (first angle under 45 degrees; run equals distance off when the angle doubles), four-point bearing 45/90 (run equals distance abeam), special angle pairs, dipping range approximation 2.08 x (sqrt height of light + sqrt height of eye). Use only to cross-check; prefer Bowditch for citations.

sources.title: Rapid radar plotting
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Six-minute plotting interval; R and M plots; extend R-M as the direction of relative motion (DRM) line; CPA is the closest the DRM line passes to own ship; TCPA by stepping off the R-M distance along the DRM; R-T-M triangle with T as own ship's 6-minute run, TM gives the target's true course and speed. Magazine article: paraphrase only.

sources.title: TimeZero Professional user guide: ARPA target
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. ARPA in TimeZero needs a heading sensor and radar; manual acquisition or automatic guard zones (Ethernet radar only); up to 200 targets; icon states; CPA/TCPA and proximity alarms. Gear-skills track only; there is no sign TC examines any software brand.

sources.title: Master Limited (under 60GT) Certificate of Competency
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. BC provider listing for Master Limited under 60 GT: 2 months sea time on vessels of at least the same GT after age 16, age 18 at issue; five courses: MED Domestic Vessel Safety (formerly A1/A2), ROC-MC, Marine Basic First Aid, Chartwork and Pilotage Level 1, Navigation Safety Level 1; then the TC oral exam; scope 'Master on any vessel less than 60 GT of a type, tonnage, area and period of operation specified' on near coastal Class 2 or sheltered waters voyages; program about $5,770.

sources.title: Navigation Safety Level 1 and Orals Prep
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. NS1 course plus oral preparation on Rules of the Road and navigation safety topics before the TC oral; $1,475; Ladysmith.

sources.title: Course information: Master Limited, 60 Gross Tonnage and Less
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Describes Master Limited as a limited ticket for a single vessel or type, with examiner-added restrictions; requires Domestic Vessel Safety MED, ROC-M or ROC-MC, SVOP only for small tenders with passengers, Marine Basic First Aid, courses or challenge exams in CP1 (12 days; chart projections, TVMDC, Canadian buoyage, latitude/longitude, fixes by range/bearing/depth, time-speed-distance, electronic aids) and NS1 (6 days; collision avoidance, COLREGs, watchkeeping, lights, distress and fog signals); 60 days commercial sea time signed off by the certified master; marine medical (the provider says valid medical; MPR requires it only for passenger vessels); in-person oral seamanship exam that may cover any course topic or anything else the examiner deems necessary (CSA, stability, emergencies, vessel systems, navigation regulations).

sources.title: CP1 Chartwork and Pilotage Level 1 (course page)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. 12-day course in Part A theory and Part B practical; stated as a prerequisite for Master Limited under 60 GT, Fishing Master 4, Mate 150 GT and Watchkeeping Mate Fishing; minimum age 18.

sources.title: Oral Exam Prep Course
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Oral prep for Master Limited under 60 GT and other certificates: exam structure and technique, vessel operations, emergency procedures, collision regulations, bridge resource management, marine safety, watchkeeping, pollution prevention, leadership scenarios; prerequisites include MED and NS/CP training at the certificate level.

sources.title: ROC-M Restricted Operator Certificate - Maritime (course page)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. One-day ROC-M course for operators and crew on pleasure and/or commercial vessels within 25 miles of shore; provider says it is required for SVOP, Master Limited 60 GT and most deckhands; covers VHF, DSC, procedures, phonetic alphabet, weather broadcasts, GMDSS. Conflicts with WMI listing ROC-MC; see brief.

sources.title: Chartwork and Pilotage, Level 1 (CP1), NAU 038
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. 12-day CP1 course supporting Master Limited (60 T), Fishing Master IV, Mate 150 GT and Watchkeeping Mate Fishing; students write the TC CP1 exam on the final day; $1,650.

sources.title: Master Limited under 60 GRT (NAUT 1480)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. 9-week course: chartwork and pilotage for coastal navigation, COLREGs, local waters, basic shiphandling, pollution prevention, master's duties in grounding, collision and fire, hands-on radar and electronic position fixing; outcomes include chart symbols, plotting positions, variation/deviation/compass error, radar and GPS, buoyage, current calculations, shiphandling, stability, emergencies.

sources.title: Master Limited 60 GRT (NAUT 1475)
sources.edition: Course content 'effective as of Winter 2005'; accessed 2026-10-06
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Outcome list: chart terms and abbreviations, projection effects, Canadian aids, plot latitude/longitude, bearing and range, course and distance, magnetic compass construction, variation and deviation, deviation card, compass error by transit, magnetic vs gyro, time-speed-distance, laying courses, DR and EP, tide and current predictions, set/rate/drift, leeway and current, course to steer, course and speed made good, fuel for a coastal passage; COLREGs with Canadian modifications; guidance for officers in charge of a navigational watch. Useful as a CP1-level checklist.

sources.title: MARI 0257 Master Limited Under 60 Gross Tons (Exam Prep) Online
sources.publisher: Georgian College, Centre for Marine Training and Research (Owen Sound, ON)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser (also the course list page https://www.georgiancollege.ca/marine-training/marine-courses/master-limited-exam-prep-mari-0155/). 80-hour exam prep; lists TC requirements: marine medical if passengers, Marine Basic First Aid, MED DVS, ROC-M or ROC-MC depending on area, SEN Limited if the vessel has radar, two months sea service on a vessel of similar size. The SEN Limited item is not in MPR s. 131 (it is in s. 130 for 60 GT or more).

sources.title: NS1 Navigation Safety Level 1 (Transport Canada exam course)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. NS1 covers the Collision Regulations, STCW Code Chapter VIII, international light, shape and sound signals and bridge teamwork procedures; the TC exam is 2 hours, 100 multiple-choice questions at 1 mark each; recommends at least three weeks of preparation.

sources.title: CP1 Chartwork and Pilotage Level 1 (Transport Canada exam course)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. The TC CP1 exam is 3 hours: 10 multiple-choice questions worth 3 marks each and 5 practical chartwork questions worth 5-15 marks each; a non-phone calculator is required; candidates may challenge CP2 instead.

sources.title: CP1 - Chartwork and Pilotage 1 (Transport Canada exam guide)
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. Study-guide (retailer) page: says CP1 is required for the 150 GT Mate and the over-60 GT Master (silent on under 60 GT); topics: chart construction and types, publications, buoys and fog signals, chart symbols (Chart 1), compass to true conversion, use of instruments, tide calculations (says none have appeared on tests so far); tools: parallel rules and dividers. Source of the noted conflict.

sources.title: Master Limited Practical (Transport Canada exam guide) and Over 60GT Master Limited certificate page
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser (with https://www.nauticalmind.com/blog/transport-canada-exam-guide/certificates/over-60gt-master-limited/). The Master Limited oral/practical is the culminating exam, taken only after sea time, courses and written exams; may be held aboard the vessel the certificate will apply to, with manoeuvring and emergency drills; topics: safety procedures, emergencies (fire, flooding, MOB, abandonment, collision, grounding), ship's systems (electrical, plumbing, propulsion), shiphandling, communications (on board, ship to ship, distress), pollution prevention, passenger safety, cargo safety; points to TP 2293 (2007) section 12.11, pages 169-179. Over-60 page lists CP1, NS1, SM2 and the oral/practical.

sources.title: Domestic Vessel Safety, MED DVS
sources.notes: Read via automated summariser. MED DVS replaces the old MED A1 and A2; minimum 26 hours over 3 days; for small commercial, passenger, workboat and fishing crews on domestic voyages; topics: hazards, fire chemistry and extinguishing, emergency response and alarms, life-saving appliances and abandonment, cold water survival, rescue, distress signals, passenger control. How DVS maps to the MPR s. 131 MED wording (basic safety; small passenger vessel safety) should be confirmed against TP 4957.
